clue.text: He's sponsored superior seating cricket side added

parts.note: the gods are the highest, cheapest seats in a theatre's gallery
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A cricket club adds a smart stand to its ground as a sponsored project.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GODS is British theatre slang for the top gallery; 'added' just joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A child presented at baptism has a godparent who acts as sponsor, so this boy has been sponsored.

clue.text: Rock drummer's penultimate taunt

parts.note: the Rock is the nickname of Gibraltar, shortened to Gib

indicators.note: penultimate means next to last, so the second-to-last letter of drummer is taken

explanation.surface: A rock drummer's second-last remark is a jibe at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music but is Gibraltar, commonly called Gib in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibe is a mocking remark, the same thing as a jeering taunt.

clue.text: Crisis gripping Switzerland's former capital

indicators.note: gripping means holding on to, so one piece is clasped inside the other

parts.note: a drama is an exciting or tense crisis
CH is the international code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A crisis takes hold of the Swiss city that used to be the seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts you toward a city, but it means money: the Greek currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the Greek currency until the euro, so it is money that is no longer in use.

clue.text: Paris's father in extravagant amateur musical

indicators.note: in places the French word for father inside the other letters

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, meaning extravagant
in Paris a father is called pere in French

explanation.surface: Paris's dad takes part in a lavish amateur stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the city here, not the Trojan prince, so his father is French; 'in' places it inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light comic opera, a kind of musical stage work.

clue.text: Communicators briefly suffering setback during Great Plague

indicators.note: during places one stretch inside the other

parts.note: epic means great or heroic in scale

indicators.note: a setback sends the shortened word backwards
briefly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the media are the means of communicating news

explanation.surface: Messengers reeling from a reversal in the time of the Great Plague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Plague' looks like one phrase but splits. 'briefly' drops the last letter of the communicators, 'suffering setback' turns them round, and 'during' sets that inside the word for great.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease, just as a plague is.

clue.text: Like Mum and Dad, I complain vigorously about doctor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the doctor
vigorously suggests the letters being shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protesting loudly about the family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vigorously' rearranges I COMPLAIN to PALINOMIC, and 'about' puts it round DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum and Dad each read the same forwards and backwards, which is what a palindromic word does.

clue.text: Mistrusts the French leaving for a short time during game of tennis

indicators.note: during sets the single letter inside what remains
leaving signals that the French article departs from the tennis game

parts.note: doubles is tennis played two a side
le is the French word for the
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Suspicions about whether a French pair left a tennis match early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the French article out of the tennis game, leaving DOUBS, and 'during' sets the time letter among what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt someone is to have no faith in them, so the verbs match in sense and form.

clue.text: Bill often gets here in armour leading fight

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the armour comes before the fight

parts.note: chain mail is flexible armour of linked rings
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A knight in armour takes the lead in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person's name but is an invoice, which the postman drops in.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters and bills arrive by post into the box at the door or gate, so a bill often ends up there.

clue.text: Fruit cut up primarily to feed players

indicators.note: to feed means to go inside, as food goes into the mouth

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
hewn means cut, as with an axe

indicators.note: primarily means first, taking the opening letter

explanation.surface: Chopped-up fruit is handed out first to the members of a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' reads as one phrase, but 'cut' gives HEWN and 'primarily' takes U from 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the cashew is the kernel of a fruit, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Shameless supporter of female branch of religion

parts.note: a bra is a woman's supportive undergarment
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A backer of a women's wing of some faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a fan, but here it is an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen describes someone bold and unembarrassed, lacking any sense of shame.

clue.text: Emperor's declaration of independence welcomed by Santa's other half

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Santa Claus is the full name, and Claus is its second half
UDI is a unilateral declaration of independence, as Rhodesia made in 1965

explanation.surface: A ruler announces his freedom and is greeted by Mrs Claus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other half' reads as a spouse, but it is the second half of the name Santa Claus.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudius was a Roman ruler who reigned from AD 41 to 54.

clue.text: I catch extremely blasé felons on the run

definitions.text: I catch extremely blasé felons on the run

indicators.note: on the run suggests things scattered and fleeing, so the letters are rearranged
extremely means at the extremes, taking the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A senior police officer boasts of nabbing casual criminals who have fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes B and E from 'blasé'; 'on the run' rearranges them with I CATCH FELONS. The whole clue is also what such an officer might say.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a British police force is the officer whose job is catching runaway criminals.

clue.text: Lethargic spectator from Chesterfield apt to shuffle over?

parts.note: a chesterfield is a padded leather sofa

indicators.note: to shuffle is to mix up, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A sleepy viewer on a sofa from the town of Chesterfield, likely to roll over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shuffle' rearranges APT TO into POTAT. Chesterfield is also an English town, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lounges in front of the television all day is an idle watcher, a sofa-bound viewer.

clue.text: On cruise, this paper, not the Scotsman, can be a lifesaver

parts.note: to coast is to cruise along without effort

indicators.note: not means without, so the Scotsman is taken out of the paper

parts.note: this paper is the Guardian, where the puzzle appeared
Ian is a typical Scottish first name, standing for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: On a cruise ship, this newspaper rather than The Scotsman might save your life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scotsman is also a real newspaper, so the surface plays two papers against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastguard patrols the shore and rescues people in danger at sea.

clue.text: Drop in yield

definitions.meaning: to pay someone a casual visit
to be won over and change one's mind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in yield' reads as falling output, but it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both paying a casual call and being persuaded to agree.

clue.text: Available power replaced by ten draught animals

indicators.note: replaced by signals one letter being swapped out for another

parts.note: open means available, as a post open to applicants
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Available power has been swapped for ten beasts of burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draught' is not beer but pulling, as in hauling a plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated cattle used to pull carts and ploughs are classic animals of traction.

clue.text: Distinctive copper bar put up to support drill

indicators.note: to support means to sit underneath, so in this down entry the rest comes below

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercise drill
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means written upwards, reversing the word

parts.note: a rail is a horizontal bar

explanation.surface: A distinctive copper bar is raised to hold up a power drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' looks like a tool but is gym exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar means characteristic of one thing alone, marking it out as different.

clue.text: This leads to masses of tiny holes

definitions.text: This leads to masses of tiny holes

indicators.note: leads to means the leading letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A creature that ruins woollens by leaving them full of little holes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the opening letters of its last four words spell the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes moth larvae eat wool and leave fabric peppered with tiny holes.

clue.text: What's old country's top navigator brought back?

definitions.text: What's old country's top navigator brought back?

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, reading the letters backwards
top means the first letter

parts.note: John Cabot was an Italian-born explorer who sailed for England in 1497

explanation.surface: A quiz question about what an early explorer brought home from the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses O, C and CABOT together. The whole clue also defines the leaf that explorers brought back from America.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco was carried from the Americas to Europe by early voyagers.

clue.text: Legislative body funds facility for night-time relief

parts.note: a chamber is a house of a parliament
a pot is a pool of money

explanation.surface: A parliament's money pays for a late-night amenity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' sounds like aid, but it is relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel kept under the bed is used to urinate during the night without going to the toilet.

clue.text: Working girl with key turned up and nosed around

parts.note: a pro is slang for a prostitute, euphemistically a working girl

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A woman arrived with a key and snooped about the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a door, but it is the delete key on a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move stealthily about, poking and searching like a predator.

clue.text: Knight with lustrous clothing rises and prepares to 22, maybe

indicators.note: rises in a down entry means read from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed
clothing means wrapping round, so the shiny word goes about the chess piece

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight in shining armour stands up and gets ready to pray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' puts N inside SLEEK; 'rises' reverses the lot. 22 refers to the answer to 22 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone going down on their knees is often getting ready to say a prayer.

clue.text: Sailor wrecked Cambridge college rowers, so they say

parts.note: Robinson College is one of the colleges of Cambridge University

indicators.note: they say means spoken, so the words sound like the needed letters

parts.note: a crew is a team of rowers; so gives SO

explanation.surface: Students rowing for a Cambridge college have suffered a wreck, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Robinson College is a Cambridge college founded in 1979. 'crew, so' spoken matches the castaway's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's hero is a mariner left on an island after his ship goes down.

clue.text: Run in to return petition

indicators.note: in signals the single letter going inside the other word

parts.note: pay can mean return, as in what a job gives you
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone rushes in to hand back a written appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'petition' looks like a noun but is the verb: to ask earnestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray is to make an earnest request or plea, as a petitioner does.

clue.text: US mother turning back on her brothers, perhaps

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a mother's brothers are her children's uncles

indicators.note: turning back means reading backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An American mum turns her back on her own brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' looks like a modifier but is the whole definition: the country's personification.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a top hat personifies the United States government.

clue.text: Stalwart's reviewed rent — everyone included

indicators.note: reviewed read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so the letters run backwards
included means taken inside the other word

parts.note: a rip is a tear or rent in cloth
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter's rent has been reassessed with everything taken into account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for housing but means a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar of the community is a dependable, staunch supporter.

clue.text: Abandons dodgy element of play at Wimbledon

parts.note: to drop something is to abandon it
hot can mean stolen, hence dodgy

explanation.surface: Giving up on a dubious feature of the tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis tournament, so 'play' is tennis, not theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A softly struck tennis ball that falls just over the net is a shot used in matches.

clue.text: When to eat fish caught in Wear?

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the fish goes into the other word

parts.note: to fray is to wear thin at the edges
id is a variant spelling of ide, a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A question about when to eat fish taken in the River Wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Wear flows through Durham, but here 'Wear' is a verb. 'fish' does double duty, also finishing the definition 'When to eat fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians traditionally ate fish rather than meat on the fifth weekday.
